title: Contrastive Meta-Learning for Few-shot Node Classification

problem.claim: Few-shot node classification must predict node labels using only limited labeled nodes as references.

gap.claim: Existing meta-learning approaches address label shortage, but the model must support both intra-class and inter-class generalizability of node embeddings.

contributions.claim: The work proposes COSMIC, a contrastive meta-learning framework for graphs.
COSMIC uses contrastive two-step optimization in each episode to align node embeddings within the same classes.
COSMIC generates hard node classes through a similarity-sensitive mix-up strategy to strengthen inter-class generalizability.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe COSMIC as a novel contrastive meta-learning framework and identify two key designs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on prevalent few-shot node classification datasets reportedly verify the framework's effectiveness.
The authors report that COSMIC outperforms other state-of-the-art baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Few-shot node classification addresses graph mining tasks with limited labeled nodes.
Existing work generally uses meta-learning episodes to transfer knowledge from classes with abundant labels to classes with limited labels.
The central objective is learning node embeddings that generalize across classes, requiring both within-class alignment and between-class discrimination.
COSMIC addresses both forms of generalizability through contrastive episode optimization and similarity-sensitive hard-class mix-up.
Experiments on prevalent datasets are reported to show effectiveness and superiority over state-of-the-art baselines.

source_observation.claim: The framework separately targets intra-class alignment and inter-class discrimination.

interpretation.claim: Few-shot representation learning may benefit from explicitly addressing both compactness within classes and separability between classes.

application.claim: When designing few-shot graph classifiers, consider pairing within-class alignment objectives with hard or similarity-aware class construction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these design choices transfer beyond the reported graph datasets or tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the contrastive optimization or mix-up strategy.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
